findings.message: This host did not provide a verified exact author model for the planning review.

I found no blocking defects in the 12 scenario blocks. They compile to 17 cases (4 + 6 + 2 + 4 + 1), which matches the census in the Work Log. Every numbered Rule R1–R5 has at least one scenario that would fail if its feature were missing or always returned the same answer. The rejection scenarios pair with success scenarios that actually tell the two cases apart: R2's complete-proof demo, and R4's outline rows that expect current success. Variations not covered here have named lower-level matrices in dimensions.md. All scenarios carry the declared @surface.safeword-cli tag and run through the real CLI. None asserts an out_of_scope or non-goal outcome. The ticket has no parent, so there are no inherited boundaries to check. I have four non-blocking warnings: the Killer Demo is split across two scenarios, refused-path non-authority is proved only at lower level, the unmapped-case scenario needs a test seam that could conflict with R1's fixed-contract rule, and the retry scenario's When step includes its own outcome.

Killer Demo proof is split. The Payoff has two halves: verifiable evidence with complete named results and exact inputs, and the historical ledger staying visibly unfinished with no completion authority granted. The @demo scenario 'Complete fixed-lane execution produces verifiable current evidence' proves only the first half. The second half is proved by the untagged R5 scenario. The Payoff is not left unproved, so this is not a coverage gap. However, the demo by itself does not show the release story. Suggested fix: add an And step to the @demo scenario saying the result grants no RED, certification or completion authority and the historical ledger stays unfinished. Alternatively, record why the demo is split.

R5 says 'Both successful and refused observations identify their execution-evidence-only meaning.' Only the successful path is an acceptance scenario. The refused and interrupted cases are planned through the extended lower-level matrices observer-history-preservation and observer-recovery-messages in dimensions.md. That is an acceptable binding, but the implementation plan must make sure those matrices assert the execution-evidence-only label on actual refused CLI results. Checking only the internal record type would not prove the claim.

Possible proof-boundary conflict in the R2 scenario 'An unmapped delivery case prevents execution'. R1 requires the case mapping to come from the observer's reviewed, shipped contract, and a caller or project-edited census must never be able to change it. To produce an unmapped case through the real CLI, the test needs a fixture shipped contract or build-time profile. The implementation plan should name that seam. If the seam is a runtime override available to callers, it would weaken R1's fixed-contract invariant.

In 'Retrying an interrupted attempt preserves the failed evidence', the When step reads 'retries ... successfully', so the step includes its own outcome. Put the passing-lane condition in the Given (for example, 'and the fixed lane now passes for the candidate'). Then the When is the retry request alone and the successful new attempt becomes an observable Then.

R4's outline tells changes apart well. Its rows require different outputs: stale for semantic source or scope edits, current for Work Log or audit-only writes. An implementation that always answers stale or always answers current fails at least two rows. The scope-change row correctly asks for review of an updated shipped contract instead of a plain rerun.

The retry-retention scenario starts from a saved nonempty diagnostic and asserts it is byte-for-byte unchanged and does not verify as success. That closes the earlier vacuous-retention gap. The lower-level observer-persistence controls for deletion, truncation and identity reuse cover the other mutations.

The mid-run candidate-change scenario and the outline for absent, skipped and failed required assertions each vary one dimension and keep the same outcome shape. Missing a case to assertion mapping is a pre-execution refusal, while failed proof refuses success after the run. These two failure classes are correctly kept in separate scenarios.
